issues.description: The template's dd_simulation.py imports a compute-table object named CT from dd.py, but the template dd.py defines the compute table instance as _CT (leading to an import/name mismatch). The solution repository defines CT (no underscore). This naming mismatch will cause ImportError/name resolution failures and prevents students from using the compute table as intended.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the compute-table instance name consistent. Either rename _CT to CT in the template dd.py (preferred) or change the import and all references in dd_simulation.py to use _CT. Keeping the name CT (without underscore) matches the solution and avoids import errors.

issues.description: The template decision-diagram module and the simulation module use inconsistent identifiers for the shared compute-table instance: template dd.py defines the compute table as `_CT`, while the template dd_simulation.py imports `CT`. The reference solution defines `CT` (no underscore). This mismatch will confuse students and cause import/runtime errors when following the template implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the compute-table identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename `_CT` to `CT` in the template dd.py (or adjust the import in dd_simulation.py to `_CT`) so that both the template and solution use the same name `CT` for the ComputeTable instance.
